title: Proteome-wide identification of the druggable CRBN interactome - Nature Biotechnology
gist: By pairing a yeast protein-complementation screen (GluePCA) with an AI surface-similarity search (MaSIF-mimicry) over 75,684 AlphaFold2 human protein domains, the authors show ~210 zinc fingers plus 43 novel non-zinc-finger proteins already bind CRBN in the presence of plain pomalidomide without being degraded — tripling the known putative molecular-glue target list. A follow-on 960-compound screen converted one such latent binder, RNF39, into a genuinely degraded target, demonstrating the binder-to-degrader path end to end.

themes.theme: Latent binders as the drug-discovery asset

insights.claim: The core thesis is that proteins which already bind CRBN in the presence of a generic molecular glue like pomalidomide, but are not degraded, are the highest-value starting points for degrader development, because prior work shows only a two- to threefold increase in binding affinity converts a bound protein into a robustly degraded one.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Reframes degrader discovery from phenotypic screening to affinity engineering on a pre-mapped binder list — a fundamentally cheaper and more systematic pipeline for any targeted-protein-degradation company.
insights.quote: reporting that an approximately two- to threefold increase in target binding to CRBN–MGDs suffices to convert CRBN–MGD-bound proteins into robustly degraded ones24,26
insights.locator: We hypothesize that many proteins found to be degraded

insights.claim: For CRL4 E3 ligases, target lysine availability is not the limiting factor for degradation because lysines make up roughly 8-15% of surface-exposed residues and the ligase is mobile; binding affinity is the actual lever.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Removes a commonly cited biological objection to degrader tractability, widening the plausible target universe to essentially any protein that can be made to bind tightly enough.
insights.quote: target lysine availability is generally not seen as a limiting factor, given the mobility of the ligase54,55
insights.locator: Our binding-focused interactome reveals a broad set

insights.claim: Low-affinity, non-degradative CRBN binding events are not expected to consume E3 ligase flux, so the large latent interactome does not create a competition or toxicity problem for existing drugs.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Defuses the safety concern that a promiscuous binder landscape implies off-target degradation liability for marketed IMiDs.
insights.quote: While high-affinity substrates are effectively cleared, low-affinity, non-degradative binding events are not expected to impact the flux of CRBN E3 ligase58.
insights.locator: Our binding-focused interactome reveals a broad set

themes.theme: GluePCA: yeast growth as a cheap binding assay

insights.claim: GluePCA converts molecular-glue-induced protein binding into yeast growth by splitting a methotrexate-resistant murine DHFR into DH and FR fragments fused to CRBN and candidate proteins, giving a pooled, sequencing-readable interaction assay at thousands-of-variants scale.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: A generalizable, low-cost platform for mapping induced-proximity interactomes that competes directly with mass-spec-based CRBN interactome mapping on cost per data point.
insights.quote: The binding between the proteins reconstitutes DHFR activity, allowing yeast growth to serve as a proxy for interaction
insights.locator: GluePCA measures compound-dependent ZF binding to CRBN

insights.claim: GluePCA growth rates reproduced published biophysical IC50 rankings for CRBN-Ikaros complexes (ZF1-ZF2-ZF3 ~460 nM, ZF2-ZF3 ~470 nM, ZF2 alone ~73,540 nM) without any protein purification.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: If a yeast growth curve substitutes for purified-protein biophysics, the cost floor for degrader triage collapses by orders of magnitude.
insights.quote: GluePCA thus provides a rapid and sensitive readout of MGD-induced CRBN binding, matching the dynamic range of biophysical assays while eliminating the need for protein purification.
insights.locator: Next, we assessed the dynamic range of the assay

insights.claim: Screening 8,363 individual C2H2 zinc fingers across 1,407 genes plus 5,293 tandem dual zinc fingers across 713 genes yielded 201 single-ZF and 285 dual-ZF dose-dependent pomalidomide binders, confirming earlier predictions that more than 100 zinc fingers are compatible with CRBN-pomalidomide binding.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: The zinc finger family, historically considered undruggable, has a confirmed 200-strong druggable subset — a target list, not a hypothesis.
insights.quote: These findings experimentally confirm previous predictions that more than 100 ZFs are compatible with CRBN–pomalidomide binding, with top binders being subjected to degradation24.
insights.locator: Encouraged by these results, we expanded GluePCA

insights.claim: The screen recovered 9 of 11 previously reported degraded zinc fingers and additionally captured SALL4, a validated pomalidomide target that earlier single-ZF degradation screens had missed.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Binding-based screening has strictly higher recall than degradation-based screening — degradation readouts systematically miss real targets, a methodological edge worth pricing.
insights.quote: Among the top binders, we also identified SALL4, a validated pomalidomide target15,16, which eluded previous single-ZF degradation screens24.
insights.locator: Comparing our data with published single-ZF degradation screens

insights.claim: Two previously unreported pomalidomide-recruited zinc fingers, ZNF852 and ZNF341 (a STAT3-regulating transcription factor), showed robust degradation in cellular reporters with plain pomalidomide.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: New off-target degradation events for an already-marketed drug class; ZNF341-STAT3 has immunology relevance worth tracking for both efficacy and safety.
insights.quote: We also identified previously unreported pomalidomide-recruited ZFs: ZNF852 and ZNF341, a TF regulating STAT3
insights.locator: Overall, the top dual-ZF hits aligned with the single-ZF screen

insights.claim: REST, a transcriptional repressor implicated in multiple cancers, binds CRBN-pomalidomide as a single zinc finger but is only degraded when the adjacent ZF3 is present, proving that flanking accessory zinc fingers, not just the contact ZF, gate degradation.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Construct design determines whether a target scores as a hit — prior negative degradation screens using single domains are unreliable and worth re-running.
insights.quote: While REST ZF2 alone was not degraded, the dual ZF2–ZF3 construct was degraded in the presence of pomalidomide
insights.locator: Furthermore, we observed that REST, a transcriptional repressor

themes.theme: Degron architecture: main and accessory zinc fingers

insights.claim: A deep mutational scan of 89,918 single-point mutations across 124 dual-zinc-finger binders showed one dominant 'main' ZF whose mutation is most deleterious, with the neighbouring 'accessory' ZF able to either enhance or reduce binding.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Provides a mutational map for rationally engineering selectivity, and shows the degron is a two-part system rather than a single motif.
insights.quote: For most constructs, one ZF was dominant, and mutating this ZF showed the most deleterious effect on binding
insights.locator: CRBN–pomalidomide recognizes a three-consecutive-ZF degron

insights.claim: Cryo-EM structures at 3.5 A resolution of SALL4 and Ikaros bound to DDB1-CRBN with pomalidomide establish that the functional degron can span up to three consecutive zinc fingers in an accessory-main-accessory arrangement.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Degron definition must be widened from one ZF to three, which changes how target-prediction libraries and computational searches should be constructed.
insights.quote: we conclude that the aZF N- or C-terminal of mZF can comprise up to three consecutive ZFs (aZF–mZF–aZF)
insights.locator: On the basis of the SALL4 and Ikaros structure

insights.claim: The SALL4 cryo-EM map revealed an extra alpha-helix C-terminal to the main zinc finger, absent from prior crystal structures but predicted by AlphaFold2, and its presence strengthened binding roughly 1.4-fold.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: AlphaFold-predicted secondary structure elements outside the canonical degron carry measurable binding energy — a cheap source of affinity gains in compound design.
insights.quote: Single-clone GluePCA assays showed that the presence of the helix strengthened binding ~1.4-fold
insights.locator: We observed additional density located C-terminal of mZF2

insights.claim: Accessory zinc finger binding modes are non-conserved and neomorphic, so unlike the relatively conserved main ZF binding mode they cannot be inferred from evolutionary sequence conservation.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Explains why sequence-homology and coevolution-based AI tools underperform here, and why surface-geometry methods were needed instead.
insights.quote: While the mZF binding mode is relatively conserved, the aZF contributes through multiple and apparently non-conserved binding modes in line with a neomorphic, evolutionary non-conserved, binding mode.
insights.locator: In addition, our DMS screen suggests that the aZFs

insights.claim: WIZ is flagged as an exception whose widely separated zinc finger domains act independently, indicating degron architectures exist beyond the three-ZF and two-ZF-plus-helix motifs described.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: The degron taxonomy is not closed — screening frameworks that assume tandem architecture will systematically miss a class of targets.
insights.quote: Exceptions such as WIZ12, which contains ZF domains widely spread apart acting independently, highlight diverse degron architectures
insights.locator: Mechanistic analyses revealed that ZFs engage CRBN

insights.claim: The Helios-specific degrader ALV2 achieves selectivity by a dual mechanism: it enriches Helios and the related Eos while simultaneously causing a significant drop in enrichment for nearly all other zinc fingers in the library, including Ikaros, ZNF692 and SALL4.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Selectivity is designed by active exclusion, not just affinity gain — a concrete design principle for next-generation glue chemistry and a testable metric for evaluating competitors' selectivity claims.
insights.quote: Hence, ALV2 selectivity involves stabilizing the target and destabilizing the remainder of the ZF interaction space.
insights.locator: The molecular basis of specificity for CRBN-based degraders

insights.claim: The 3.6 A cryo-EM structure of CRBN-ALV2-Helios shows selectivity is mediated through the accessory ZF1: Helios residues I122, N125 and V129 contact CRBN while S133 contacts the compound, and a V129A mutation ablates the interaction entirely.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Single-residue dependencies at the accessory interface define both potency and resistance liability — the mutational escape route for a Helios degrader is now explicitly mapped.
insights.quote: in single-clone GluePCA, we found that mutation of I122A, N125A and S133A reduced binding, while V129A ablated the interaction
insights.locator: While ALV2 affinity is achieved by accommodating Helios H141

insights.claim: SALL4 and ZNF692 are excluded from ALV2 binding by predicted steric clashes between the compound and their accessory zinc fingers, with ZNF692 carrying a leucine (L413) where Helios has the critical ALV2-engaging serine (S133).
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Gives a residue-level rule for predicting which zinc fingers a given optimized glue will spare — directly usable for off-target risk assessment.
insights.quote: with leucine (L413) replacing the critical Helios serine (S133) that engages ALV2
insights.locator: Superimposing other ZF–CRBN structures, such as ZNF692

insights.claim: Optimized molecular glue scaffolds can be surprisingly clean in targeting select zinc fingers, whereas classical IMiDs appear intrinsically promiscuous.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Undercuts the assumption that glue degraders are inherently dirty — selectivity is a chemistry problem that has already been solved once, supporting the modality's therapeutic-index case.
insights.quote: Our data for ALV2 binding indicate that the MGD scaffolds can be surprisingly clean in tageting select ZFs for binding
insights.locator: Growing out the compound toward the ZF

themes.theme: AI surface mimicry beats sequence and co-folding

insights.claim: The team built a searchable database of 75,684 human protein domains from AlphaFold2 predictions and compared surfaces with MaSIF-mimicry, a modified MaSIF-seed pipeline scoring surface similarity rather than complementarity.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: A reusable proteome-scale asset: any newly solved ligase-substrate structure can be re-queried against the same 75,684-domain surface index in a single run.
insights.quote: This yielded a database of 75,684 human protein domains.
insights.locator: Human proteome surface fingerprint database

insights.claim: AlphaFold3-style co-folding was explicitly rejected as the discovery engine because it is computationally too expensive at proteome scale and struggles to predict novel glue-mediated ternary complexes, partly due to the absence of evolutionary constraints in neomorphic interfaces.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: A concrete published limit on the highest-profile structure-prediction models for induced-proximity drug discovery — surface-descriptor methods, not co-folding, are the working tool in this domain today.
insights.quote: State-of-the-art co-folding methods, such as AlphaFold3, are computationally expensive to scale at the proteome level and struggle to predict novel MGD-mediated ternary complexes47, partly owing to the absence of evolutionary constraints in neomorphic interfaces.
insights.locator: Proteome-wide prediction of CRBN targets using surface mimicry

insights.claim: Surface-based MaSIF similarity discriminated known CRBN zinc finger substrates far better than full-length sequence similarity, interface pseudo-sequence similarity, ESM2 protein language model embeddings or structural similarity metrics.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Protein language model embeddings underperform geometry-based surface descriptors on induced-proximity interface prediction — a directional signal on where AI-for-biology value actually sits.
insights.quote: Other homology-based metrics (for example, sequence similarity, interface pseudo-sequence similarity, ESM2 embedding distances or structural similarity) showed far weaker discrimination
insights.locator: We benchmarked MaSIF-mimicry using the single-ZF library

insights.claim: The apparent promiscuity of CRBN is explained not by a loose binding site but by the widespread recurrence of a similar surface pattern across the human proteome, implying a largely unexplored latent interactome.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Recasts CRBN's substrate breadth as a mappable, enumerable property rather than an unpredictable liability — the basis for treating the ligase as a programmable platform.
insights.quote: the apparent promiscuity of CRBN can be attributed to the widespread presence of a similar surface pattern across the proteome, while also suggesting the existence of a largely unexplored latent CRBN interactome
insights.locator: We next expanded the search space to the entire human proteome

insights.claim: An Ikaros-interface query returned 110,356 poses above a 0.4 MaSIF similarity score across 25,947 structural domains predicted to bind CRBN-pomalidomide in an Ikaros-like manner.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: The computational candidate pool is five orders of magnitude larger than what has been tested — the experimental screen, not the prediction, is now the bottleneck.
insights.quote: identified 110,356 poses with a MaSIF similarity score >0.4 and template modeling (TM) score <0.5, corresponding to 25,947 structural domains predicted to bind CRBN–pomalidomide in an Ikaros-like manner
insights.locator: Synthetic DNA library design

insights.claim: The method retrospectively recovered known neo-substrates found by other techniques, including CHD7 and PPIL4 from mass spectrometry, NEK7 and MNAT1 from proximity ligation, plus VAV1 and mTOR, with predicted binding modes matching experimentally resolved structures.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Retrospective recovery of orthogonally discovered targets is the strongest available validation that the computational pipeline generalizes rather than overfits.
insights.quote: Among these computational hits, several previously reported substrates were recovered, including CHD7 and PPIL4, which were found by mass spectrometry19, as well as NEK7 and MNAT1, through proximity ligation17
insights.locator: Notably, in each case, a substantial number of domains

themes.theme: New target space beyond the G-loop

insights.claim: A 'bonsai' library of 1,959 in-silico-truncated 86-residue sub-domains, filtered for stability and against transmembrane and disordered segments, yielded 43 novel plus 6 known dose-dependent CRBN-pomalidomide binders when run through GluePCA.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: A ~2.5% prospective hit rate from a purely computational shortlist is a workable funnel economics for industrialized degrader target discovery.
insights.quote: Beyond these, 43 novel protein domains showed compound-dependent binding (log2(FC) > 1.5, P < 0.01), spanning diverse protein folds with predicted similar surface signatures at the interface
insights.locator: From this Ikaros-mimicry bonsai library subjected to GluePCA

insights.claim: Several hits do not use the canonical beta-hairpin G-loop interface: SPART uses a helical G-loop and CKAP5 bypasses the critical glycine entirely, with an A-to-N mutation weakening binding as predicted.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: The G-loop motif is no longer the boundary of CRBN target space, which materially expands the addressable proteome for the entire molecular glue modality.
insights.quote: Some use helical G-loops (for example, SPART), or even bypass the crucial glycine entirely (for example, CKAP5)
insights.locator: Notably, based on MaSIF-mimicry, several of the hits

insights.claim: In an orthogonal mammalian NanoBiT split-enzyme assay, RNF39, CHD8, TDRD6 and SPART all showed compound-dependent binding abolished by the predicted G-to-N mutations, while CKAP5 failed to confirm.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Four of five yeast hits transfer to human cells; the honest CKAP5 failure marks the non-G-loop claim as the weakest link in the paper.
insights.quote: All identified proteins (RNF39, CHD8, TDRD6 and SPART), except CKAP5, do show compound-dependent binding in NanoBiT.
insights.locator: To further validate the GluePCA hits in an orthogonal assay

insights.claim: The hit set covers hard-to-drug proteins and diverse domain classes including PDZ, RRM and WW domains across kinases, plakins and helicases, spanning transcriptional regulation and cell differentiation.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Degradation reaches protein classes that small-molecule inhibition never addressed — the strategic argument for TPD platform valuations rests on exactly this breadth.
insights.quote: Many GluePCA hits found in this study represent hard-to-drug proteins52 (Supplementary Table 2); in addition, they cover a diverse set of domains, such as PDZ, RRM and WW
insights.locator: To further validate the GluePCA hits in an orthogonal assay

insights.claim: The zinc finger family screened here numbers more than 675 human members and the G-loop motif appears in more than 2,500 human proteins, quantifying the ceiling on CRBN-addressable target space.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: A concrete TAM number for the modality: thousands of proteins carry the structural feature required for CRBN engagement.
insights.quote: The majority of these contain a G-loop motif, present in more than 2,500 proteins in the human genome18.
insights.locator: In addition to ZFs, other protein classes and folds

insights.claim: The authors describe the bonsai truncation approach as a coarse pre-screen used only when intact domains or full-length proteins cannot be screened, an explicit caveat on the 43 novel binders.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Discount the 43-hit figure until full-length confirmation; the validated subset is the five proteins taken through single-clone and NanoBiT assays.
insights.quote: We consider the bonsai approach a coarse pre-screen used to validate MaSIF-mimicry predictions when the intact domain or FL proteins cannot be screened.
insights.locator: Beyond the canonical β-hairpin G-loop

themes.theme: From latent binder to real degrader: the RNF39 proof

insights.claim: Screening RNF39 against a focused 960-compound Enamine CRBN immunomodulatory analog library in NanoBiT found 0.85% of compounds gave over twofold improvement, yielding eight hits, with Z5000181945 and Z4999952733 each producing a fivefold increase over pomalidomide.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: A ~1,000-compound focused library is enough to find a 5x affinity gain on a fresh target — the chemistry step after target identification is cheap and fast.
insights.quote: In the screen, 0.85% of tested compounds showed increased binding over pomalidomide by twofold, allowing us to identify eight compounds that robustly enhanced the RNF39–CRBN interaction relative to pomalidomide
insights.locator: GluePCA hits are privileged entry points for novel MG discovery

insights.claim: SAR from the eight hits favours the 5-position exit vector on the phthalimide-isoindolinone core with short planar linkers, ureas outperforming amides, and hydrophobic aromatic substituents, while longer linkers reduce activity.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Directly actionable medicinal-chemistry rules for anyone building CRBN glue libraries against novel targets.
insights.quote: the exit vector is favored at the 5-position of the phthalimide–isoindolinone core and with short, planar linkers, with ureas outperforming amides
insights.locator: An analysis of these eight compounds suggests

insights.claim: Z5000181945 induced actual degradation of the RNF39 RING finger domain, rescued by the NEDD8-activating enzyme inhibitor MLN4924, confirming the degradation is cullin-RING ligase dependent and on-target given a G-to-N mutant abolished the induced binding.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: The full computational-prediction to validated-degrader loop was closed inside a single paper, which is the key de-risking event for the whole workflow's commercial claim.
insights.quote: Furthermore, Z5000181945 also induces degradation of the RNF39 RING finger domain, which is rescued by the NEDD8-activating enzyme (NAE) inhibitor MLN4924
insights.locator: The Z4999952733- and Z5000181945-induced interactions were abolished

insights.claim: The authors claim the identical MaSIF-mimicry plus GluePCA workflow is fully portable to any other E3 ligase molecular glue complex for which target structures are available.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Platform rather than single-asset value: the same pipeline could map VHL, DCAF and other ligase interactomes as their structures land.
insights.quote: We anticipate that the identical workflow is fully portable and can be applied to other E3 ligase MGD complexes for which target structures are available.
insights.locator: In summary, we present an integrated workflow

insights.claim: The zinc finger screen alone tripled the number of known putative CRBN targets, with more than 210 zinc fingers identified as dose-dependent binders in a family typically considered undruggable.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Quantifies the step change in the target list — a 3x expansion in the discovery substrate for every company working the CRBN modality.
insights.quote: we identified more than 210 ZFs as CRBN–MGD binders in a dose-dependent manner, tripling the number of known putative targets
insights.locator: Using the ZF family as a first test case

insights.claim: Author N.H.T. is a founder and shareholder of Zenith and Serac Therapeutics and a consultant to Ridgeline Discovery, with the laboratory receiving financial support from AstraZeneca, Sanofi, Merck KGaA and the Novartis Foundation, while B.L. is a founder, shareholder and employee of ALLOX.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: The workflow is already wired into at least four private degrader ventures and four large pharma sponsors — the commercialization path is pre-built, and these are the names to watch for licensing or partnership news.
insights.quote: N.H.T. is a founder and shareholder of Zenith and Serac Therapeutics as well as a consultant to Ridgeline Discovery. The laboratory receives financial support from AstraZeneca, Sanofi, Merck KGaA and the Novartis Foundation.
insights.locator: Competing interests

insights.claim: The authors position GluePCA's overexpression format as an advantage over recent proteomic approaches like IP-MS, TurboID and ProxyCapture because it guarantees candidate presence in the cell and permits complete mutational control for validation.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Frames the competitive landscape for interactome mapping: expression-independent screening versus native-abundance proteomics is the axis on which platforms will be compared.
insights.quote: GluePCA, by virtue of being an overexpression format, assures that candidate proteins are present in the target cell, including complete mutational control of the interactions for validation and perturbation.
insights.locator: Recent proteomic approaches, including IP-MS

insights.claim: Even where the same scaffold cannot degrade a hit, the authors argue these binders remain promising optimization starting points, citing mTOR which they found as a pomalidomide binder but which is only degraded by a different molecular glue.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Sets expectation management: a binder list is a chemistry starting point, not a drug pipeline, and each entry still needs a bespoke compound campaign.
insights.quote: these scaffolds represent promising starting points for future compound optimization
insights.locator: Although the same MGD scaffolds may not degrade many such proteins
